claims.statement: PolicyLM trainable parameter count (tied embedding counted once)

PolicyLM architecture: width 128, 2 pre-LN blocks, 4 heads, feed-forward width 512, dropout 0.1, vocabulary 282 tokens, maximum program length 640 tokens; context prefix from a 2-layer MLP; LM head tied to the token embedding; three heads (q, three-class feasibility, runtime) on the end-of-sequence state concatenated with the context embedding
Context vector: 2,051 values from one pinned pretrained tabular encoder (2,048 pooled hidden values plus 3 query diagnostics)
Input normalizer: means and scales frozen from training contexts only, zero scales set to one, standardized inputs clipped at +/-10
Program catalog used for constrained decoding: 6,640 programs drawn only from training-context teachers (catalog sha256 116154767f2d...)
Optimizer: AdamW, learning rate 3e-4, weight decay 0.01 (biases and norms excluded), gradient-norm clip 1, plateau control halves the rate (patience 5) down to a floor of 1e-6
claims.value: lr 3e-4; wd 0.01; clip 1; x0.5, patience 5, floor 1e-6
claims.tex: AdamW, $\eta_0{=}3{\times}10^{-4}$, weight decay $0.01$, clip $1$, halving with patience $5$ to floor $10^{-6}$

claims.statement: Batching: up to 16 training contexts per update with at most one context per parent lineage; micro-batches capped at 8,192 padded tokens without truncation; per-context window of up to eight measured candidates plus an eligible teacher
L6 objective coefficients: CE 1.00, Bradley-Terry 0.25, listwise 0.10, q regression 0.25, feasibility 0.10, runtime 0.05
Physical checkpoint: 10,751,892 bytes holding 48 model tensors, 144 AdamW state tensors and the CPU and CUDA random states
v1: each optimizer update durably emits two proposals, one for a rotating training context and one for a rotating validation context (v2: see C134)

Score definitions: robust scale s_c = 1.4826 MAD, else IQR/1.349, else SD; eps_c = max(1e-12 max(1,|mean y|), 1e-6 s_c); q = -1/2 sum_j log(max(RMSE_j,eps)/max(base_j,eps)) over two inner folds; q_opt = clip(q, +/-log 1000); q_grid = round-half-even(1e6 q)
Execution timeout 90 s; runtime is regressed as log1p(seconds) and a timeout is right-censored at log1p(90)

Ranking-pair weight min(|dq_opt|, 1), doubled when either program sits at or above the 0.9 within-context midrank percentile; listwise term needs at least 3 measured programs; Huber delta 1; teacher and list temperatures 0.25

Anchored step (form exact_trie_kl_eval_mode_v1): the frozen L6 micro-batch step line for line, then weight 0.2 times the exact chain-rule KL over every branching node of the deployed catalog prefix tree (end of sequence included, deployed child mask, temperature 1.0) on the batch's first context, policy in evaluation mode (no random draws), policy pass with activation checkpointing per 16,384-token chunk, anchor pass without gradient, then the frozen clip/step tail; reported loss stays the L6 total; anchor is the frozen v1 terminal policy loaded read-only from the sealed capture and shared with the KL guard

Two objective identities: training_objective_sha256 = digest({schema jope.v2-training-objective/v1, l6, anchor_kl}) = 1c0c050f877b576ac37fc54842ecf3cbd17d44641af81c9320c87e639453a55e for the real capture, bound in the config, campaign identity, genesis, every batch proof, progress, terminal intent, verification and result (roots without it are refused); the target contract objective_sha256 stays the L6 label objective bf02f87341bc52aa4b3c329492d1eae5621c3543a9e60c9b3f34aa7b407ece48

At the anchor the anchor KL is exactly 0; its gradient leaves a float64 rounding residual (|g| up to about 3e-17) that the accumulated clipped gradient and AdamW absorbed: parameters, both AdamW moments, step, random state and clip norm bitwise equal to the frozen L6 step in the fixtures and in the R23-build GPU parity probe; an observed property, not a structural guarantee

Merged regression guard (G32): at every closed epoch the latest fixed-panel validation L6 is compared with the sealed v1 reference 0.8705178834 (v1 plateau best on the fixed panel); 3 consecutive closed epochs strictly above 1.02 times the reference trip it; a good epoch resets the count before a trip; the trip is sticky, holds adoptions while training continues, is sealed in every verified closure and recovered only from the seal; each closed epoch is checked exactly once

Merged KL guard (gap T12): at every closed epoch, first in the boundary and before any side effect, the exact catalog KL from the current policy to the v1 anchor on 64 digest-chosen training probe contexts (validation and outer-test never probes), with a leaf-closure check at 1e-9; alarm at mean >= 0.03 (non-blocking); sticky hold at mean >= 0.05 or maximum >= 0.15; deadline checked at entry, after every chunk and probe and before returning; an unfinished probe defers the whole boundary with no state change; sealed in every verified closure; history capped at 50

Verified-watermark custody: each closed epoch chain-verifies planner and outbox events from the previous watermark head and joins each committed step to its proof bytes, durable acknowledgement row and outbox emission event with continuous counts; before any clean closure and resume every committed proof is re-hashed against planner-chain evidence and the proof filename set must equal the committed steps exactly

Tick-safe stop and ordered terminal closure in the merged learner: reservations only when the remaining in-loop time covers the bounded step budget; segment record before any reservation; terminal intent first, then suffix joins and full indexed verification inside a closure budget, then the verification record (binding intent, watermark, heads, control, checkpoint, execution and guard states), then the result; any error publishes a closure-failure record and no clean result; resume refuses missing, stale, failed or rebound closures

Overlay admission in the merged package: overlay records are CE-false; the builder never certifies itself; after the build returns the caller writes one create-only acceptance envelope pinning marker bytes, packet, receipt, the unchanged paired bound, a post-return sample and physical evidence; the bounded publisher fsyncs and links a publication candidate and rechecks the bound; an operator records a return witness; consumers require envelope, candidate and witness for every packet and never rely on the absence of a refusal; the envelope is unsigned; durability fixtures are toy-scale CPU worlds, not hardware power-loss qualification

Closed-epoch inbox in the merged learner: at startup (closed epoch) and after every closed epoch the learner reconciles the inbox and adopts at most one candidate; a hold keeps training on the active snapshot; a refused inbox stops the run; prepared roots are consumed only with their operator acceptance envelope; a second fresh authority proof is taken after hydration and rechecked inside the compare-and-swap

CLOVER direction (2026-10-12; a research proposal, not an approved implementation or demonstrated improvement): CLOVER-Discover, a qualified program-discovery engine with conventional offline search, reproducible execution, independent semantic checks and controlled evaluation, must be useful with no neural controller and is the foundational architecture; CLOVER-Learn, a learned evaluation-allocation controller, is accepted only when controlled experiments establish incremental benefit over Discover

CLOVER hypotheses: H1 qualified offline search repeatedly finds useful programs outside the 6,640-program catalog; H2 a learned selector beats conventional selection on identical candidate pools; H3 fresh verified outcomes beat frozen models, offline replay and optimizer restarts; conditional H4 learned guidance improves the search's own candidate generation; if only H1 holds, keep a verified discovery engine and claim no reinforcement-learning flywheel

CLOVER claim rule: no self-improving reinforcement-learning claim until fresh feedback causally improves independently confirmed selection beyond the strongest non-learning baseline; PolicyLM, outcome distillation, edit-gain modelling, RLOO/PKPO and preference optimization are candidates, not commitments, and compete only after a simple outcome-predictor ranking proves useful

CLOVER phases 0-5 are gates, not commitments (0 comparability, 1 useful support expansion, 2 ranking learnability, 3 fresh-feedback value, 4 guided discovery, 5 independent qualification and handoff), with no requirement to advance through all; Phase 0 foundations (experiment identity, quantile/parity and label-visibility audits, fail-closed hold/recovery) merged in PR #296

When support expands, CLOVER requires an approved reference distribution with positive probability on the new support and a new versioned stability protocol; the old catalog-only KL threshold cannot automatically be reused
PolicyLM is treated as one candidate model, not the assumed winner; the v2 learner is therefore a CLOVER-Learn candidate
The CLOVER synthesis rejects L6 as the success metric; L6, preference loss, KL compliance and novelty must not stand in for search performance
claims.tex: L6 is not a success metric
